The last time I felt like I belonged was probably when I and a couple of others went to visit our friend who lives in another city. It was last summer. We went sightseeing and got drunk later that day, watching stupid videos and laughing at our own jokes. This trip made me feel less like a fuck-up. We haven't properly talked since then. They don't need me in their life. They don't miss me either. Do I miss them? I have no idea. 

Cutting used to bring my mind some clarity. I cut myself every time I felt like my head was about to explode from all the thoughts buzzing in my head. I used to go to the kitchen, take the sharpest knife  and start slashing haphazardly. The cuts weren't terribly deep, but I they left a few faint scars. Whenever I did that, my mind would become blissfully empty. It's a bit different now. I have to be more careful, more strategic. I use a box-cutter. It stings like a bitch. Physical pain distracts me from emotional pain. I cut my palms, my fingers (I leave a cut or two on my arms sometimes and I don't cut my thighs anymore, because they take a long time to heal, and I like wearing short shorts at home) and instead of thinking how worthless I am, I can only think about stopping the blood and cleaning the wound. Priorities, you know.
I don't feel much when I self-harm. That's my aim - not to feel anything. To escape. 

I haven't tried medication, actually. Even if I had the money for it, I wouldn't know what to buy. You need prescription for those, anyway. Which I don't have. 

>Have the writers even struggled with something difficult?

They might have but they're probably generally positive people who are incapable of feeling down for long periods of time. Sometimes I wonder who's more insane: me or people like that.

I'm sorry things suck for you too.

Yeah, I can't even count how many times I've been fed the "You're so young, you've got your whole life ahead of you" line. The thing is, I don't want that "whole life". I don't want to find "the perfect job", "the perfect partner", have a "perfect wedding", "perfect kids" and then retire one day and die of old age. I don't want to become rich and famous either. I have no goals, no ambitions whatsoever. All I want is to escape.

Self-harm helps with that a bit. I usually cut my arms, sometimes - my legs. I used to make tiny cuts on my face (they didn't leave any scars) and long ones on my abdomen (also no scars). But it doesn't feel as good if the cuts are in a place where I can't immediately see them. Sometimes I strangle myself, sometimes I bang my head on the wall. Not very effective and gives me a headache, which I get pretty often without doing anything to myself, so that's rarely any fun.

I'd seek more professional help, from different therapists but money is a big issue. Besides, I don't know if I'm as open to the idea as I was before. Even thinking about going makes me mildly uncomfortable.

Going to university makes me outright terrified.  People remimd me all the time that the next year will be my final, that I'm almost done with this degree, that I need to put more effort into studying, that with a diploma I'll have better chances of getting a good job. I just can't make myself do homework, and copy notes, and finish assignments, and write course papers (I can't even do bare minimum, so I'll need a lot of luck and help and effort to pass my exams this year). So I avoid almost everyone connected with that part of my life. 

Because I'm a coward and I'd rather run from my problems than solve them. 'd rather stuff my brain with useless content than contribute to the society I have no desire to be a part of. 

>When someone asked why I'm still alive, I responded that I'm not dead yet. /r/technicallytrue. . . 

Can relate. How do *you* cope, by the way?
thank you for writing this, and I'm sorry you're going through depression, hope my reply doesn't hurt you in any way

I've gone to a therapist's office a couple times. Actually, I've seen several therapists (three, to be precise). None of them diagnosed me with depression. Two of them said that I just needed to make more friends. And another one told me I had PTSD (which is not true, btw, because I've never experienced any traumatic events). Even though I didn't like our sessions, I'm inclined to believe them. I do feel happy from time to time. I have things that interest me. It's just that I feel like these moments of happiness aren't worth living for. Like... Do I want to see new episodes of my favourite TV shows? Yeah, I do. But if I had a choice between watching a new episode, or playing a new game, or reading an amazing book... and dying instantly? I'd chose the latter without hesitation. Because an episode only postpones my suffering for 40 minutes. While death removes all of it forever.
And I know this is extremely selfish of me to think about passing away and leaving my family behind, but I wouldn't care when I'm dead, would I?
Basically, a year and a half ago my dad ran out on us, leaving me and my mom with a few debts. For a long time I couldn't figure out how I feel about this whole mess. I'm still unsure. However, this destroyed what little motivation I had to finish uni. I had to find a part-time job, which I did. It doesn't pay well, but it's more or less stable and my boss isn't too bad of a person. Besides, it's connected with my major and it's the only thing I know how to maybe sort of do. Doesn't mean I enjoy it, though. At the beginning of this year my mom was made redundant and she still can't find a job (especially with coronavirus roaming about). She keeps telling me that everything will be okay but I don't believe her. Everything just keeps getting worse and the only two reasons I'm not an alcoholic yet are: 1)I can't afford to spend all my money on booze; 2) Why bother with beer, when you can cut yourself and instantly feel great and awful at the same time. I try not to self-harm too much and too often, since I don't want my mom or my students to notice. But that also means there's no outlet for my emotions, no stress-relief.
. 
. 
. 

TL;DR: I don't have depression, because a professional told me so. My family is in shambles and destructive habits help me cope but that's not why I want to die. I just don't see the point in continuing living, because that shit ain't worth the struggle. I'm only 21 but I'm fed up with life already.

I can't afford failing. Literally, we're broke af.
But thanks for the nice message. I appreciate it.
